title.narrative: Building Peaceful Coexistence Between Rohingya Refugees and Hosts by Gender Responsive Development Initiatives for CSOs

description.narrative: Overall Objective:Peaceful coexistence, social cohesion, and resilience among Rohingya and host communities are improvedOutcome:Vulnerable and marginalized groups from Rohingya and host communities in Teknaf and Nhila, Cox's Bazar, benefit from adequate social services and economic opportunities with improved representation through 300 civil society organizations working on conflict sensitivity, gender advocacy, and livelihoods.

The direct target groups (4,500–5,000 people, half of whom are women) come mainly from Teknaf Union, Cox's Bazar, in particular from Rohingya camps 24, 25, 27 and the nine districts in the neighboring Nhila Union (75% Rohingya and 25% Bangladeshi residents of the host communities).The proposed project also directly targets 300 civil society organizations (approximately 16 members per CSO, with 50% women). Civil society organizations include women-led groups, forums for people with disabilities, and youth groups working in the areas of gender and conflict sensitivity, social cohesion, human rights, capacity building, and climate change.As the proposed project will be implemented in the same geographical area as P5421, some of the participants in the previous project will also be involved in this follow-up project. This applies in particular to cases where the project participants continue to be members of groups established under P5421, such as CPGs, youth clubs, and RVMV groups, as they too will benefit from the capacity-building activities planned under this proposal. Furthermore, the capacity development components that are part of the proposed project differ significantly from the activities of the P5421 program, which will result in a different composition of civil society organizations and project participants.

The protracted Rohingya crisis in Cox’s Bazar has intensified socio-economic pressures, leading to conflicts between refugees and host communities over limited resources. Women and girls from both groups are particularly vulnerable. Civil society organizations (CSO) in Bangladesh, however, face capacity challenges due to restricted civic space, limiting their ability to drive social cohesion and development efforts. This project seeks to strengthen CSOs, enabling them to lead gender-responsive peacebuilding and development initiatives, reduce community conflicts, and support skills-based livelihood opportunities for both Rohingya refugees and host communities. By capacitating CSOs, the project aims to foster social cohesion, build community resilience, and enhance sustainable development.
